children: Healthy exports and rising public investment have raised expectations for Germany's economic growth this year, a leading economic-research institute said Thursday.
The Ifo Institute now anticipates growth of 1.4% in 2026, from 0.8% in its previous quarterly report made in June.

"Significant impetus from abroad and increased spending on infrastructure, climate, and defense in Germany are preventing a more severe economic slowdown due to the energy-price shock and low water levels in rivers," Timo Wollmershaeuser, head of business cycle analysis and forecasts at the Ifo, said.

The uptick was also driven by an upward revision to gross domestic product growth in 2026 so far. In late August, Germany's statistics agency said growth in the second quarter was 0.3%, better than the 0.2% first reported, driven by stronger exports that overcame some of the hit from surging energy costs due to the war in Iran. GDP increased 0.4% in the first quarter of this year.
The damping effects of the energy-price shock on the economy now look weaker, Ifo noted.
"There are rays of hope, especially for the crisis-stricken industry sector," Wollmershaeuser said. Industrial output has climbed in recent months, official data showed.
"The German economy is continuing to recover," he added.
The Ifo now expects growth at 1.2% in 2027, up from the 0.8% it predicted in June, and at 0.8% in 2028.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel told French daily Le Monde on Wednesday that growth is on track for roughly 1% this year, better than the central bank's June forecast. The central bank had, however, previously warned that heatwaves would temporarily slow the economy over the summer, particularly as low water levels hinder river transport including through the Rhine River.

Nagel is a member of the European Central Bank's governing council, which is expected to vote to raise the key interest rate by a quarter-point next week. The Ifo said inflation is set to rise to 3.0% next year, and won't move back toward the ECB's 2% target until 2028.
